messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Click and drag to change the filter parameters
messages.description: You can change the filter parameters by clicking and dragging on theobject's display. By default, horizontal mouse dragging is mapped to cutoff frequency, and vertical mouse movement is mapped to gain (ifis enabled). If the cursor is located directly over the edge of a filter band, however, the band rectangle is highlighted, indicating that clicking and dragging will map x-axis movement to adjust filter bandwidth instead of cutoff frequency. .If multiple bandwidth regions are overlapping, you can cycle through them by double-clicking on the topmost one. This is useful for accessing smaller bandwidth regions that might be otherwise "covered" by a larger region.

messages.name: allpass
messages.digest: Set the filter type to allpass mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to allpass mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency, or cutoff frequency) gain, and Q (resonance), although only the gain parameter has an effect on the amplitude response. An allpass filter is designed to modify the phase response (use themessage to view the phase response).

messages.name: analog
messages.digest: Enable analog filter prototype for bandpass/peaknotch filters
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by aor, toggles the analog filter prototype parameter for the bandpass, and peaknotch filters. Unlike the standard digital versions, these "imitation analog" filters do not have a notch at the nyquist frequency, and thus imitate the response of a analog filter. The imitation analog filters are slightly more computationally expensive, so this option is set to 0 (disabled) by default.

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: Allows for backwards compatibility with obsolete messages
messages.description: Allows for backwards compatibility with these obsolete messages:,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,, and.

messages.name: bandpass
messages.digest: Set the filter type to bandpass mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to bandpass mode. It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency) gain, and Q (resonance).

messages.name: bandstop
messages.digest: Set the filter type to bandstop mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to bandstop mode. It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency) gain, and Q (resonance).

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Report internally-stored biquad coefficients
messages.description: In left inlet: In display mode,causes theobject to send its internally-stored biquad coefficients out the leftmost outlet. In the interactive filter modes,additionally causes the current filter parameters to be sent out their respective outlets (see Output).

messages.name: cascade
messages.digest: Set the filter to cascade display mode
messages.description: In left inlet: Themessage works in display mode only. The word, followed by up to 24 groups of five float values corresponding to filter coefficients, will display a composite filter response which shows the multiplication of a group of biquad filters in cascade.

messages.name: constraints
messages.digest: Constrain the frequency, amplitude and Q values within a specified range
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by seven numbers, allows you to constrain the frequency, amplitude and Q values within the specified ranges. This is useful to constrain values obtained by clicking and dragging. The first number should be an integer, and it specified the filter number whose constraints will be set. The remaining six numbers are floating-point values which set the minimum and maximum frequency values, the minimum and maximum amplitude values, and the minimum and maximum Q values, respectively. Specifying constraint values of zero will remove the constraints for that value. Themessage causes the filter coefficients to be output.
messages.argPattern: filter-index:int, minimum-frequency:float, maximum-frequency:float, minimum-gain:float, maximum-gain:float, minimum-Q:float, maximum-Q:float

messages.name: dictionary
messages.digest: Use adictionary's filter coefficients
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that references a namedobject dictionary, will cause theobject to use the dictionary values for filter coefficients.

messages.name: display
messages.digest: Set the display-only mode for the.
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to display only. It is equivalent to themessage. In display mode,simply displays the frequency response for a set of fivefilter coefficients.

messages.name: displaydot
messages.digest: Enable display of the mousable bandwidth region in display mode
messages.description: In left inlet: Themessage, followed by aor, toggles the display of the mousable bandwidth region whenis in display mode. This allows you to useas an interface to design and display your own filter algorithms. The default is disabled (by default, display mode functions uniquely as a display).

messages.name: flat
messages.digest: Enable flat response (no resonance for filtering)
messages.description: The word, followed by a list that specifies the indices of filters in a multifilter array, will set the designated filters to flat response (i.e. no resonance for filtering) The changes made to the filters vary depending on filter type:Lowpass and highpass filters: Q values set to 0.707, and gain coefficients are set to 1. (0dB)Band pass and band stop filters are ignored.All other filter types: The gain coefficients are set to 1. (0dB)

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In 1st-5th inlets: When in display mode, a float in one of the first five inlets changes the current value of the corresponding biquad~ filter coefficient (a0, a1, a2, b1, and b2, respectively), recalculates the filter's frequency response based on these coefficients and causes a list of the current filter coefficients to be output from the leftmost outlet.In 6th inlet: Sets the center or cutoff frequency parameter for the filter and causes output.In 7th inlet: Sets the gain parameter for the filter and causes output.In 8th inlet: Sets the Q (resonance) or S (slope) parameter for the filter and causes output.Note: Input to any one of the inlets will recalculate the current filter's graph and trigger the output.

messages.name: gainmode
messages.digest: Set gain parameter for the lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and bandstop filters
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by aor, toggles the gain parameter for the lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and bandstop filters. The traditional definitions of these filters have a fixed gain of 1.0, but by gain-enabling them, their amplitude response can be scaled without the additional use of a signal multiply at the filters output.The default is 0 (disabled).

messages.name: highorder
messages.digest: Display the response of an nth order filter
messages.description: Themessage works in display mode only. The word, followed by a list of n groups of biquad filter "a" coefficients and n-1 groups of biquad filter "b" coefficients, will display the response of an nth order filter.

messages.name: highpass
messages.digest: Set the filter to highpass mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to highpass mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (cutoff frequency) gain, and Q (resonance) or S (slope - used for the shelving filters).

messages.name: highshelf
messages.digest: Set the filter to highshelf mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to highshelf mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (cutoff frequency) gain, and S (slope).

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: Allvalues are converted to.In 1st-5th inlets: When in display mode, a float in one of the first five inlets changes the current value of the corresponding biquad~ filter coefficient (a0, a1, a2, b1, and b2, respectively) for the selected filter in the UI, recalculates the filter's frequency response based on these coefficients and causes a list of the current filter coefficients to be output from the leftmost outlet.In 6th inlet: Sets the center or cutoff frequency parameter for the selected filter in the UI and causes output.In 7th inlet: Sets the gain parameter for the selected filter in the UI and causes output.In 8th inlet: Sets the Q (resonance) or S (slope) parameter for the selected filter in the UI and causes output.Note: Input to any one of the inlets will recalculate the current selected filter in the UI's graph and trigger the output.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: A list of five float values which correspond tofilter coefficients sets theobject's internal values for these coefficients and causes the object to output the list out its left outlet. Ifis in display mode, it will display the frequency response of the filter obtained from these coefficients. If more than five values are sent, they are interpreted as sets of cascaded biquad coefficients (see themessage).in 6th inlet: A list of three values which correspond to center/cutoff frequency, gain and Q/S (resonance/slope), sets these values, recalculates the new filter coefficients and causes output. This is equivalent to themessage.

messages.name: lowpass
messages.digest: Set the filter to lowpass mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to lowpass mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency, or cutoff frequency) gain, and Q (resonance).

messages.name: lowshelf
messages.digest: Set the filter to lowshelf mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to lowshelf mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency, or cutoff frequency) gain, and S (slope).

messages.name: markers
messages.digest: Display frequency values
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a list of up to 64 frequency values will place visual markers (vertical lines) at these frequencies behind the graph. Themessage will set the markers used for both linear and logarithmic frequency displays.

messages.name: mode
messages.digest: Set the filter type
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number from 0-9, sets the current filter type. The numbers and associated filter types are.Number - Filter type0 - display only1 - lowpass2 - highpass3 - bandpass4 - bandstop5 - peaknotch6 - lowshelf7 - highshelf8 - resonant9 - allpassIn display mode,displays the frequency response for a set of fivefilter coefficients. In the other modes, it graphs the frequency response of a filter based on three parameters: cf (center frequency, or cutoff frequency) gain, and Q (resonance) or S (slope - used for the shelving filters).

messages.name: options
messages.digest: Set filter-specific options
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by five integers, allows you to set the filter-specific options for a given filter. The first number specifies the filter whose options will be set. The remaining four integers set the filter mode (message) gain-enabling flag (message), analog filter prototype flag (message) and interactive filter mode flag (message), respectively. Themessage causes the filter coefficients to be re-evaluated and output.

messages.name: params
messages.digest: Set filter parameters for the current filter and trigger output
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, when followed by three numbers specifying frequency, gain and Q, sets the filter parameters for the currently selected filter and triggers output. When followed by four numbers specifying filter number, frequency, gain and Q, this messages sets the filter parameters for the filter indicated and causes output.

messages.name: peaknotch
messages.digest: Set the filter type to peaknotch mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to peaknotch mode.It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency, or cutoff frequency) gain, and Q (resonance).

messages.name: query
messages.digest: Report amplitude and phase response for a specified frequency
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a float value, will cause the amplitude and phase response of the graph at that frequency to be sent out the sixth outlet of theobject as a list.

messages.name: resonant
messages.digest: Set the filter type to resonant bandpass mode
messages.description: In left inlet: The wordsets the filter type of theobject to resonant mode (resonant bandpass filter). It is equivalent to themessage. The frequency response of the filter is based on three parameters: cf (center frequency) gain, and Q (resonance).

messages.name: selectfilt
messages.digest: Highlights a specific filter
messages.description: Highlights a specific filter in the UI. To switch to a filter to edit it, use.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a list of five int values which correspond tofilter coefficients, sets theobject's internal values for these coefficients but does not cause output. Ifis in display mode, it will display the frequency response of the filter obtained from these coefficients.in 6th inlet: A list of three values which correspond respectively to center/cutoff frequency, gain and Q/S (resonance/slope), sets these values, recalculates the new filter coefficients but does not cause output. In display mode this message has no effect.
messages.argPattern: a0/center frequency:float, a1/gain:float, a2/Q:float, b1:float, b2:float

messages.name: setconstraints
messages.digest: Constrain filter values within a specified range without causing output
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by seven numbers, allows you to set the frequency, amplitude and Q constraint values within the specified ranges without causing output. This is useful to constrain values obtained by clicking and dragging. The first number should be an integer, and it specified the filter number whose constraints will be set. The remaining six numbers are floating-point values which set the minimum frequency, maximum frequency, minimum amplitude, maximum amplitude, minimum Q and maximum Q, respectively. Specifying constraint values of zero will remove the constraints for that value.
messages.argPattern: filter-index:int, minimum-frequency:float, maximum-frequency:float, minimum-gain:float, maximum-gain:float, minimum-Q:float, maximum-Q:float

messages.name: setfilter
messages.digest: Select a filter in a multiple filter array
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, specifies the filter, by number, which is the currently selected filter in a multiple filter array. Filters are numbered from 0.

messages.name: setoptions
messages.digest: Set filter-specific options without causing output
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by five integers, allows you to set the filter-specific options for a given filter without triggering output. The first number specifies the filter whose options will be set (filters are numbered from 0). The remaining four integers set the filter mode (message) gain-enabling flag (message), analog filter prototype flag (message) and interactive filter mode flag (message), respectively.

messages.name: setparams
messages.digest: Set filter parameters for the current filter without causing output
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, when followed by three numbers specifying frequency, gain and Q, sets the filter parameters for the currently selected filter without triggering output. When followed by four numbers specifying filter number, frequency, gain and Q, this messages sets the filter parameters for the filter indicated, without triggering output.

messages.name: whichfilt
messages.digest: Specify a currently edited filter without display highlighting
messages.description: Selects a specific filter as the one actively being edited (without highlighting it in the display).
